title: Criminal trespass vs house trespass - the practical difference
p1:
Not every illegal entry into a property is treated the same under criminal law.

Many people think walking into someone’s house without permission is simply “trespassing”. But the law draws a sharper line that can change the seriousness of the offence.
p2:
The surprising part: house trespass is actually a more specific form of criminal trespass.

Criminal trespass generally means entering or remaining on someone else’s property with the intention to commit an offence, intimidate, insult, or annoy the person in possession. House trespass goes one step further — it involves entering a building, tent, or place used for human dwelling or custody of property.
p3:
A person entering an empty plot unlawfully may face criminal trespass charges. The same act of entering someone’s home without permission can become house trespass because the law gives greater protection to living spaces.

The practical takeaway: the location of the entry matters, not just the act of entering.
conclusion: Did you know that the same unauthorised entry can attract different legal consequences depending on whether it happens on open land or inside a house? Share your thoughts.
